blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (Ruralz Control upgrades, Upgrade order, Figure 2)
blocking.issue: The Raft rules freeze wire and storage encodings at N-1 until finalize. They do not freeze rendering semantics. While binaries are mixed, Ruralz Control keeps building Revisions from Git. If minor N changes a `ruralz/v1alpha1` default, which line 75 allows, one commit renders to different digests depending on whether an N or an N-1 replica leads. An election mid-upgrade can therefore produce a different Revision, spurious Drift or an unplanned Rollout, and the new default reaches N-1 Nodes before the operator finalizes. Figure 2 also resumes pushes from an N CLI before finalize ('i' comes before 'h'). The N CLI computes the expected digest with N defaults. If N binaries rendered with N-1 defaults until finalize, which is what the encoding rule implies, that push fails with RZ-CFG-027. An operator cannot tell which defaults are in force between the last replica swap and finalize.
blocking.evidence: Line 163: "While the cluster version is N-1, every replica writes only N-1 encodings in log entries, snapshots sent to followers and the write-forwarding and status-forwarding classes on 8092, whichever replica leads, so an election mid-upgrade is harmless." Line 171: "Pushes pause from the backup until the CI CLI runs N". Figure 2: "g -- yes --> i", "i[Pin the CI ruralz CLI to N; resume pushes]", "i --> h". Line 148: "N-1 only if N's release notes list no `ruralz/v1alpha1` default change".
blocking.fix: Add rule 2a under Ruralz Control upgrades: "While the cluster version is N-1, every replica renders Revisions with the N-1 schema levels and defaults, so a commit yields the same digest whichever replica leads; N defaults take effect only after the version-advance entry." In Figure 2 and in Upgrade order, move 'Pin the CI ruralz CLI to N; resume pushes' after the finalize node ('h'): "Pushes pause from the backup until finalize, then resume from a CI CLI at N."

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (Ruralz Control upgrades, Upgrade order)
blocking.issue: The upgrade path depends on 'N decodes only N-1 encodings', but nothing guarantees that only N-1 encodings are left when the next upgrade starts. After a finalize from N-2 to N-1, the latest Raft snapshot and the retained log entries can still hold N-2 encodings until a new snapshot is taken and the log is compacted. Audit segments and other digest-addressed content on replicas are immutable and keep their original encoding indefinitely. The document's own recommended maintenance window runs two single-minor steps back to back. An N binary that restarts in the second step can then restore an N-2 snapshot, or replay N-2 entries, that it is not required to decode. Contributors implementing the Control Store cannot tell which encodings N must read.
blocking.evidence: Line 163: "N binaries MUST decode every N-1 log entry, record and snapshot." Line 171: "Ruralz Control upgrades one minor at a time, since N decodes only N-1 encodings". Line 264: "An operator can plan one maintenance window every 6 months (target) and stay supported; it contains two single-minor steps". Foundation pack section 2, Control Store row: "plus digest-addressed Revision content and audit segments on Ruralz Control replicas".
blocking.fix: Extend rule 3: "After the version-advance entry, every replica takes a snapshot and truncates its log, so no N-1 log entry or snapshot remains; the next upgrade MUST NOT start until every replica reports a snapshot at the current cluster version." Add: "Immutable Control Store content (Revision content in `ruralz.canonical.v1`, audit segments) carries a version marker, and every release decodes every marker back to the first release, or the migration entries rewrite it." Add this precondition to Figure 2 (a check before 'd' for the second step).

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (Ruralz Control upgrades, step 4)
blocking.issue: The rollback path after finalize understates what a restore does, compared with the owning document. Control plane and GitOps says restore runs only into an empty deployment and needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key, which opens a higher `storeEpoch`. It also invalidates sessions and API tokens. Unless an operator supplies a revocation list, no Node certificate issued before the restore is admitted, so every Node serves detached, not only the Nodes enrolled since the backup. An operator who follows this step during an incident will find the whole fleet detached and the CI tokens invalid.
blocking.evidence: Line 165: "After it, rollback means `ruralz control restore` from the first backup, losing every later Control Store write (Rollouts, audit entries, Enrollments); Nodes enrolled since re-enroll." Control plane and GitOps, Backup, restore and `postgres`: "`ruralz control restore` runs only from the host CLI into an empty deployment. Before any delivery it needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key, opening a higher `storeEpoch` ... It invalidates sessions and API tokens and re-applies an operator-supplied revocation list; without one, no Node certificate issued before the restore is admitted ... Those Nodes serve detached."
blocking.fix: Rewrite step 4: "After it, rollback means `ruralz control restore` of the pre-upgrade backup into an empty N-1 deployment ([Backup, restore and `postgres`](../architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md#backup-restore-and-postgres)): it loses every later Control Store write (Rollouts, audit entries, Enrollments), needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key, invalidates sessions and API tokens, and admits existing Nodes only once the operator supplies a revocation list; until then every Node serves detached, and Nodes enrolled after the backup re-enroll." Add the same warning next to the finalize node in Figure 2.

blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (Ruralz Control upgrades step 3, Figure 2)
blocking.issue: Finalize is gated on every voter reporting N. The skew table puts any N-1 binary outside policy after finalize, and Raft non-voters also apply every committed entry. OQ-system-overview-16 keeps a non-voting regional Ruralz Control open, Planned (M4), so the procedure as written lets an operator finalize while an N-1 non-voter still replicates the log. That replica then cannot decode the version-advance entry or the migration entries that follow it.
blocking.evidence: Line 164: "Once every voter reports N and a 24-hour soak (target) has passed, an operator finalizes". Line 146: "N-2; an N-1 binary after finalize" (outside policy). Figure 2: "g{Every voter reports N?}". Foundation pack 8.13: "Whether it has its own Control Store, is a Raft non-voter or is a read-only relay is OQ-system-overview-16."
blocking.fix: Change step 1 to "each replica, voter or non-voter, reports its binary version" and step 3 to "Once every replica, voters and non-voters, reports N ...". Relabel the Figure 2 node to "Every replica, voters and non-voters, reports N?"

blocking.section: Semantic versioning (Versioned surfaces, Node upgrade handover row)
blocking.issue: The handover surface names a persisted `assignmentIndex`, which no other document defines. Control plane and GitOps, the owner of assignment fencing, persists the pair (`storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`) under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/`. A contributor implementing the cross-version handover format would look for a field that does not exist.
blocking.evidence: Line 63: "`${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` file lock, candidate, persisted `assignmentIndex`, Unix-socket readiness message". Control plane and GitOps: "Nodes persist the highest pair activated under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/`", where the pair is (`storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`). No document under docs/ other than this one contains `assignmentIndex`.
blocking.fix: Replace "persisted `assignmentIndex`" with "the persisted (`storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`) pair under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/` ([Control plane and GitOps](../architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md))".
